title: South Sudan MVD Readiness - DREF Final Report (MDRSS018) - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: The MVD outbreak in Ethiopia was declared on 14 November 2025, and the preparedness operation in South Sudan was implemented from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026. The suspected deaths in Kapoeta East County were reported on 23 December 2025.
analysis.location_and_population: South Sudan, specifically the high-risk border counties of Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor, and Kapoeta East County. The affected population includes border communities with frequent cross-border movement and trade with Ethiopia.
analysis.event: A suspected Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) outbreak was reported in Kapoeta East County, South Sudan, on 23 December 2025. The event was declared as a trigger for increased preparedness measures in South Sudan due to the risk of cross-border transmission from Ethiopia.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Three suspected MVD-related deaths were reported in Kapoeta East County, including two individuals with recent travel history to Ethiopia and one suspected community-linked case. However, no confirmed cases were found during the investigation. The outbreak in Ethiopia had improved, and transmission was under control.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) and Ministry of Health implemented preparedness activities in the border counties from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026. These included volunteer training, community-based surveillance, and hygiene promotion. Despite these efforts, operational challenges such as insecurity, conflict, and logistical issues affected implementation. No confirmed MVD cases were detected in South Sudan by the end of the operation.

analysis.brief_en: The South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) and Ministry of Health initiated preparedness measures in response to a suspected Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) outbreak in Ethiopia, which was declared on 14 November 2025. These efforts were triggered by the risk of cross-border transmission through population movement, trade, and pastoral migration. The operation, conducted from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026, focused on high-risk border counties including Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor, and Kapoeta East. On 23 December 2025, three suspected MVD-related deaths were reported in Kapoeta East, with two linked to travel to Ethiopia and one suspected community case. However, investigations did not confirm any cases, and one suspected alert tested negative. Despite these measures, operational challenges such as insecurity, conflict, and poor road conditions hindered implementation. By the end of the operation, no confirmed MVD cases were detected in South Sudan, and the outbreak in Ethiopia had improved, with transmission under control.
analysis.summary_en: The South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) and Ministry of Health initiated preparedness measures in response to a suspected Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) outbreak in Ethiopia, which was declared on 14 November 2025. These efforts were triggered by the risk of cross-border transmission through population movement, trade, and pastoral migration. The operation, conducted from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026, focused on high-risk border counties including Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor, and Kapoeta East. On 23 December 2025, three suspected MVD-related deaths were reported in Kapoeta East, with two linked to travel to Ethiopia and one suspected community case. However, investigations did not confirm any cases, and one suspected alert tested negative. Despite these measures, operational challenges such as insecurity, conflict, and poor road conditions hindered implementation. By the end of the operation, no confirmed MVD cases were detected in South Sudan, and the outbreak in Ethiopia had improved, with transmission under control.

title: Five Marburg Virus Patients Recovered Following Early Antiviral and Supportive Care - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The report was published on November 19, 2026. The outbreak was declared in late October 2025, and the five survivors were admitted and managed between November and December 2025.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred in southern Ethiopia, specifically at the Jinka General Hospital Marburg Virus Disease Treatment Center. The affected population included 19 total cases, with 14 laboratory-confirmed infections and five probable cases.
analysis.event: A clinical case series documented five laboratory-confirmed survivors of Marburg virus disease in southern Ethiopia. The recovery was attributed to early diagnostic identification and prompt antiviral administration combined with supportive care.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among the 14 confirmed cases, nine individuals died, resulting in an overall case fatality rate of 64.3 percent. Five patients survived following intensive inpatient management. The disease is a severe, often lethal hemorrhagic fever with historical case fatality rates ranging between 24 percent and 90 percent.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was published in the International Journal of Emergency Medicine. The findings are based on clinical observations and treatment protocols. The case fatality rate and treatment details are explicitly stated, but the broader epidemiological context and long-term outcomes remain under investigation.

analysis.brief_en: A recent report published on November 19, 2026, by Bioengineer.org highlights the recovery of five laboratory-confirmed Marburg virus disease patients in southern Ethiopia. These patients were treated at the Jinka General Hospital Marburg Virus Disease Treatment Center during an outbreak declared by the Ethiopian Ministry of Health in late October 2025. The study, published in the International Journal of Emergency Medicine, indicates that early diagnostic identification and prompt antiviral therapy, specifically remdesivir, combined with aggressive supportive care led to viral clearance and full clinical recovery. Among the 14 confirmed cases, nine individuals died, resulting in a case fatality rate of 64.3 percent. The five survivors included four females and one male with a median age of 18 years, admitted between November and December 2025. The report notes that the disease is a severe, often lethal hemorrhagic fever with historical fatality rates ranging from 24 to 90 percent, depending on strain and clinical resources. The findings suggest that early intervention may improve outcomes, even in cases with severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage or significant hepatic injury.

title: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) Advances Galidesivir Toward Marburg Pivotal Study Under FDA Animal Rule - Kalkine

analysis.time: The news report was published on 17 November 2026. The dose-response study is set to commence in December 2026, with results expected within weeks of the observation period closing. A second study is scheduled for early 2027, with the pivotal efficacy study expected to begin around mid-2027.
analysis.location_and_population: The study involves non-human primate models in the context of Marburg virus, and the Ugandan government has approved the evaluation of Galidesivir in an active Ebola outbreak. The affected population includes individuals in Uganda during the ongoing Ebola outbreak.
analysis.event: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) is advancing its antiviral Galidesivir toward a pivotal study under the FDA's Animal Rule pathway for Marburg virus. The company has secured approvals for evaluating Galidesivir in non-human primate models and in an active Ebola outbreak in Uganda under the WHO MEURI framework.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Galidesivir has demonstrated 94 per cent survival in Marburg non-human primate models. The FDA has confirmed that it qualifies for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval. The Ugandan government's MEURI programme provides a unique opportunity to generate human safety and efficacy data in a real outbreak setting, which could support regulatory filings.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The FDA has confirmed the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for Marburg virus and has provided Orphan Drug Designation. The dose-response study is set to commence in December 2026, and results are expected within weeks. The Ugandan government has approved the evaluation of Galidesivir in an active Ebola outbreak, which is a supplementary-related entity but not the target.

analysis.brief_en: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) is advancing its antiviral drug Galidesivir toward a pivotal study under the FDA's Animal Rule pathway for Marburg virus. The company has demonstrated 94 per cent survival in non-human primate models, supporting its development for this Category A bioterrorism threat with no approved treatment in the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile. A blinded dose-response study is set to begin in December 2026, with results expected within weeks. In parallel, the Ugandan government has approved the evaluation of Galidesivir in an active Ebola outbreak under the WHO MEURI framework, offering a rare opportunity to generate human data. This initiative combines FDA-endorsed pathways, historical efficacy data, and real-world application, potentially de-risking the path to regulatory approval. The FDA has also confirmed that Galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval, adding a commercial incentive for partnerships.
